trap: the judge call raises (network/provider/timeout-shaped failure) on a run that passed every L1 check -- the run must NOT keep its PASS by default

input.task: What is the price of the Aurora Desk Lamp on this page?

provenance: M36 acceptance criterion 2 (fail CLOSED): a judge call that raises for ANY reason -- network failure, provider error, timeout, a malformed response -- must never leave a run's prior PASS standing. `judge_verdicts: ["error"]` makes `stub_judge` raise `JudgeError` on the one call this run makes, standing in for every one of those network-shaped failures at $0.00 (the fast suite cannot exercise a real timeout, so the injected exception is the offline proxy for it). This is a genuinely PASSING L1 run -- shop-lamp-std.html's Price group extraction survives every deterministic check exactly as `tc1-shop-price` (its non-mutated sibling) does -- so the ONLY thing that can turn it into `failure:semantic` is `_apply_judge` treating the raised exception as a reject rather than skipping the check. Watched red against a version of `_apply_judge` that let an exception propagate uncaught (or silently kept the prior PASS) would show `status: success` here; the committed behaviour is `status: failure:semantic`, `reason` naming 'judge unavailable, failing closed', `budgets_spent.judge_calls: 1` (the call was attempted, not skipped) and `checks.judge_available: false` (distinct from `judge_responsive: false`, which would mean the judge ANSWERED and rejected -- this run never got an answer at all).

triage.note: fail-closed is proven end to end through the real pipeline (agent.py's actual `_apply_judge`, not a mock of the whole verdict), on the same fixture/plan a normal PASS case uses, so the only variable is the judge's own failure.
